newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-IFCT steps down with FRN.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS-IFCT steps down with FRN.

text.p: Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand (IFCT) pulled its US$150 million five-year floating rate note (FRN) issue on Friday, just four days after its launch.
"I can confirm that IFCT has decided not to go forward with this issue," said one of the arrangers.
IFCT came to market on Monday with a five-year FRN with a put option at three years, and a step-up coupon.
The arranger would not say why the deal was withdrawn, but IFCT was downgraded on Wednesday by Standard & Poor's (S&P).
S&P cut IFCT's long term counterparty credit rating to A-minus from A, and its similar short term rating to A-2 (A-1).
IFCT was also downgraded late on Thursday by Thai Rating and Information Service (TRIS), which cut its senior debt rating to AA-plus from AAA.
"I think we all know why it (the deal) was pulled," one banker commented after the cancellation.
Ironically, IFCT had planned to launch in the last week of May, but decided to hold off until June, when it was hit by the S&P and TRIS downgrades.
Bankers did not expect the pulling of IFCT's FRN to affect a US$100 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue (FRCD) from Krung Thai Bank Public Co Ltd.

"Krung Thai seems to be going OK. I guess sentiment has improved a bit since the Siam Commercial Bank deal," said one banker, referring to Siam Commercial Bank Public Co Ltd's US$100 million FRCD, which was wrapped up last week.
TRIS on Thursday also downgraded debt ratings of nine Thai banks and finance firms, including IFCT, saying it expected them to face increased non-performing loans.
When Moody's Investors Service announced a review in March, a US$100 million three-year FRCD from Siam City Bank through its Cayman Island branch was postponed.
Caisse Centrale du Credit Immobilier came to the market with its US$750 million seven-year FRN, which will be listed in Hong Kong, Luxembourg and Singapore.
The issue pays a margin of five basis points over three month LIBOR, and includes put option at par after five years.
Electronics maker China Aerospace set its US$40 million three-year FRN through Deutsche Morgan Grenfel.
It guaranteed the issue, made through Casil Clearing Investment (BVI) Ltd.
The FRNs are issued at par, priced to float at 130 basis points over six-month LIBOR.
Co-lead managers get fees of 80 basis points for US$10 million or more, senior managers 65 basis points for US$5 million to US$9 million and managers 50 basis points for US$2 million to US$4 million.
The Peace Bank of Korea, a small investment bank, came out with a US$40 million three-year FRCD.
It was priced at par to pay 60 basis points over three month LIBOR, and featured put and call options in year two.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) plans to tender its twelfth issue of five-year Exchange Fund notes on June 17.
The notes carry a 6.55 percent coupon.
